$comment: Spec for scripts/defence-mutation-record.mjs. Each entry removes ONE security defence and names the single test that must then fail. `find` must occur EXACTLY once in `source` — the runner errors out otherwise, so a refactor that moves a defence breaks this loudly instead of silently scoring it green.

defences.why: clearance coupon minted from another store's dead-stock flag
purchase order raised against another store's reorder suggestion
FAQ read/write on a product owned by another store
unresolved custom domain falls through instead of 404ing (resolver defaults to a tenant)

const store = await resolveStoreByDomain(tenant);
  if (!store) notFound();

defences.why: staff can issue refunds — the orders:refund RBAC gate
login limiter's Redis failure posture flips to fail-closed, 500ing the write surface on a blip
provider refund fires on a stale order state (double refund)
out-of-band refund webhook applies refund effects on a stale order state
a replayed 'completed' webhook overwrites an already-refunded order
a retried order/refunded double-restores inventory (invents stock)
a retried order/refunded decrements coupon usageCount twice
applyRefundEffects failing after the provider refund resolves silently on the DIRECT refund path, losing the GL/inventory reversal
marketing pixels fire for a legacy/unversioned or malformed consent cookie
erased account's OneSignal player ids never reach the propagation consumer, so the third party keeps the PII
same failure on the OUT-OF-BAND refund webhook path

the guest-checkout bypass widened to exempt cookie-BEARING requests too, re-opening the lured-admin impersonation that removing isAllowlistedMerchantOrigin closed (2026-09-03 incident: 17 unpaid orders came from the opposite mistake, so both directions must stay pinned)
CSRF token stops being bound to the principal that minted it, so an attacker-minted pair replays on a victim cookie
MCP write tools (add_to_cart / place_order) commit inventory and money for any unauthenticated caller
credential resolution rejects instead of annotating, so the initialize handshake and every read tool go dark (FM-1)
any presented string authorises a write — a wrong key, and another store's key, both pass
the per-store escape hatch grants writes on every store instead of the one it was turned on for
the Express-layer tool classifier throws on a batched/null body -> next(err) -> 500 on EVERY MCP request, reads included (FM-3)
defences.find: if (message === null || typeof message !== 'object') return { tool: null, kind: 'unknown' };

POST /auth/forgot-password passes an unvalidated body value into a Prisma where, mailing a real reset link to a user the attacker never named

defences.why: an attacker-supplied X-Original-Host lands in every AI product-feed link and is cached 600s in Redis and at the CDN

the agent write credential is shown exactly once at mint; a status endpoint that also returned it (plaintext or ciphertext) would make the one-time reveal meaningless and put the secret in every admin page load

hasKey: Boolean(store.agentApiKey),
          apiKey: store.agentApiKey,
          rotatedAt: store.agentApiKeyRotatedAt,

defences.why: a revoke that only re-stamped rotatedAt would answer the same 200 and show "no key" in the admin while the old credential kept authorising MCP writes
defences.find: data: { agentApiKey: null, agentApiKeyRotatedAt: new Date() },

defences.why: the escape-hatch state shown to the merchant must never read as OPEN because the feature lookup failed — a fail-open reading of a security control
GET /stores/:id hands a whole Store row to the admin app; without the omit the agent credential ciphertext ships to the browser
the admin store list returns whole Store rows; without the omit every listed store ships its agent credential ciphertext
getBySlug writes its row into a 120s Redis cache, so without the omit the credential ciphertext is not leaked once but cached and served to every reader for the TTL
a refused agent write is recorded but nothing read the rows; if the threshold branch never fires, a broken merchant integration and a probe of the write surface both stay invisible

a merchant integration sending a stale key and someone sweeping the write surface produce the same rows; the distinct-source-IP spread is the only thing that separates them, and collapsing it pages on the wrong one at the wrong threshold
credential-less agent writes are the expected background of a published llms.txt; alerting on them at a low count is how the whole alert gets muted, and a muted alert is worse than none

an integration that predates the credential requirement cannot present a key it was never issued, so it lands in the same bucket as a crawler; folding it into anonymousFlood means the one failure this rollout actually causes is the one signature the monitor is built to stay quiet about, and the merchant learns from lost orders
a correct classifier wired to the wrong action or window is an alert that never fires, which is indistinguishable from a quiet system
the merchant page warns that writes are accepted with no key at all; a banner that renders unconditionally warns about nothing and trains the merchant to ignore it

an absent ip_address is a platform/proxy condition, not many callers; counting each as distinct relabels a merchant's broken integration as a credential sweep AND raises its firing threshold from 3 to 10, so the operator hunts an attacker while the merchant's checkout stays down

a wrong or rotated ENCRYPTION_KEY refuses every agent write on every store; reporting that as `invalid` blames the caller and makes the denial watcher classify a platform outage as a credential sweep, so the p0 that names ENCRYPTION_KEY never fires
merchant-supplied carrier baseUrl reaches fetch() unvalidated — cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 from the API host
an impersonation session deactivates the impersonated person's account via DELETE /auth/me
an attacker-controlled PUBLIC host 302s to 169.254.169.254 — the pre-flight check passes and undici follows the redirect
an impersonation session binds a new TOTP secret to a victim with no MFA and locks the owner out permanently
